research_method.claude: Quantitative questionnaire survey (7-point scale) validating a literature-derived conceptual model by PLS-SEM (SmartPLS 3); 200 emailed, 150 valid; pilot with 30 developers; five hypotheses
research_method.nlm: Quantitative survey; PLS-SEM via SmartPLS 3; 150 valid of 200 emailed questionnaires; pilot with 30 developers; five hypotheses
research_method.value: Cross-sectional questionnaire survey (7-point scale) testing a literature-derived conceptual model of knowledge work productivity with PLS-SEM (SmartPLS 3); pilot with 30 developers; 200 questionnaires emailed, 150 valid; five hypotheses, H1, H3, H4, H5 supported and H2 (efficiency strategies) not supported; R² = 0.695
research_method.note: Claude flags sign/p-value inconsistencies between Section 4.2 text and Fig. 2/Table B2 (e.g., collaboration β = -0.280 in text vs 0.280 in figure).

context.claude: Industry; software SMEs in Peninsular Malaysia (population 100, 70 randomly selected); 150 knowledge workers with >1 year experience
context.nlm: Industry; 70 SME software companies in Peninsular Malaysia; 150 developers, programmers and system analysts with >1 year experience
context.value: industry; software SMEs in Peninsular Malaysia (70 of 100 companies randomly selected); 150 knowledge workers (programmers and system analysts, >1 year experience)

data_window.note: Not stated by either (NotebookLM only says cross-sectional).

cat_productivity.note: Both tag KWP and programmer performance as Productivity, but both are perceived constructs measured by 7-point agreement items; perceived productivity goes to cat_survey per the definitions. Author may wish to review.

cat_quality.note: Both tag KWP as Productivity/Quality because the paper defines KWP as 'quality of knowledge work'; no software-quality metric (defects, code quality, etc.).

cat_collaboration.note: Collaboration construct (5 items: teamwork, trust, respect, voluntary communication); strongest path to KWP (β = 0.280 in Fig. 2).

cat_satisfaction.note: NotebookLM's 'DevEx / Satisfaction / Process' tag is on the Innovation Strategies construct (better products/processes), not a satisfaction or well-being measure.

cat_activity.note: NotebookLM tags programmer performance as Activity/Productivity, but it is a perceptual scale, not repository activity.

cat_devex.note: No DevEx framework; NotebookLM's DevEx tag on Innovation Strategies is generic.

cat_agile.note: Both tag effectiveness/efficiency strategies as 'Process', but these are perceived organizational strategy scales (scope, timeliness, resources), not sprint/workflow process metrics. Borderline.

cat_survey.note: All constructs measured by questionnaire on a 7-point agreement scale.
